what_this_is: The Nick Crown macro layer: positioning, breadth and regime read BEFORE any individual stock. It answers what kind of market this is, and therefore which family of trades is allowed today. It is deliberately separate from AQE's stock scanner and sector work.
status_means: it ran, but something was missing or on a substitute source — see limits

read_me_first.headline: A narrow market, with volatility around normal. Best fit: an inflation shock — commodities and rates up together.
why: A handful of big names are carrying the index — the average stock is falling behind.
Single stocks are moving about as much as the index. The index itself is quiet, with VIX at 15.8, lower than 77% of the past two years.
Option dealers are positioned in a way that amplifies moves — expect bigger swings in both directions than the news deserves.
Trend-following funds are mixed across the 18 markets we track, and none is at an extreme — the positioning is not crowded.
Big speculators are unusually long the dollar, the S&P, gold and 4 others; unusually short natural gas, the Nasdaq and the long bond (CFTC data to 2026-08-11).

2 warning signs lit: momentum is not keeping up with price and the crowd is already positioned this way. A further 12 showed up on individual markets. No single one of these is a reason to sell. They matter when several point the same way as the breadth reading.
read_me_first.so_what: Pair it up: short the stretched leader against the average stock. That is the closest fit rather than a clean one — 1 of its conditions are not met. Size at 0.65x your normal risk (cut because the trend is crowded).
what_would_change_it: If the 2-year trades above 103.61 (0.5% away), trend funds start buying.
If gold trades below 4,375.93 (1.0% away), trend funds start selling.
Watch for single stocks becoming more volatile while the index stays calm. That gap is the earliest warning we get.
Watch for the average stock keeping pace with the index again. That ends the leadership trade and starts the breadth trade.
This reading would strengthen if UUP down (roc5 -0.14%, roc20 -1.02%) reversed.

the_call.size_multiplier_means: Multiply the PM's OWN normal risk per trade by this. AQE does not size and does not know the book.

playbook.context: Leaders at new highs, RSI not confirming, CTA extreme.
playbook.equity: Short the diverging leader / long equal-weight or defensives
playbook.options: Bear put vertical on the leader or on QQQ

scenario.reading: INFLATION_SHOCK leads but DISPERSION_REGIME is within 12%. Two stories fit the same tape; treat the overlap as the honest read, not the winner.
scenario.story: Commodity-led repricing. Rates and the dollar rise together, which is the combination that hurts everything at once.

breadth.means: a few large names are carrying the index while the average stock lags

trend_funds.extreme_means: how crowded the trade is. High is fragile, not confident.

large_speculators.note: CFTC data covering Tuesday, published Friday, so always at least three days old. It cannot time anything.

option_dealers.means: dealers amplify moves — expect bigger swings

SPY.assumption: Customers are long calls and long puts, so dealers are long call gamma and short put gamma. This is the standard convention, NOT observed data — exchange feeds publish open interest, never who is on which side.

QQQ.assumption: Customers are long calls and long puts, so dealers are long call gamma and short put gamma. This is the standard convention, NOT observed data — exchange feeds publish open interest, never who is on which side.

volatility.gap_means: how much more the average stock moves than the index. A wide gap means the index is hiding what individual names are doing.

divergence.note: No single warning is a reason to sell. They matter when several point the same way as breadth.

what_changed: Dealer gamma flipped to NEGATIVE. Expect wider swings from here.
The allowed family changed from broadening carry to divergence pair short.

key_levels.what: Single-stock vs index gap — calm band
key_levels.if_it_breaks: Below here stocks move together and selection stops paying. Only direction matters in that regime.
Above this, protection is already expensive. A spike through it is not a fresh reason to sell.
Low correlation means stocks trade on their own news and selection pays. Rising back through the middle of its range means everything starts moving together again, and only direction matters.

how_to_read.read_me_first: The whole reading in plain English. If you only read one block, read this one. Everything else is the evidence.
how_to_read.the_call: The allowed FAMILY of trade expressions and a multiplier on the PM's own risk budget. Never a ticker, never a position, never an order. The individual setup is the PM's choice.
how_to_read.how_current: Every source with its own date. The reading is only as current as its oldest leg, whatever the generated time says.
how_to_read.scenario: Which cross-asset story best fits today. The score is the SHARE OF CONDITIONS MET, not a probability — nothing here was fitted or backtested and no base rate was measured.
how_to_read.readings: The four stages behind the call: breadth, positioning, volatility and divergence.
how_to_read.what_changed: Only the moves since the last run that would change what a PM does. An empty list means today continues yesterday.
how_to_read.what_is_coming: Scheduled moments when the reading above can change. Each carries what it tests, not a forecast.
how_to_read.key_levels: EVERY line in the sand this layer knows about, in one list sorted nearest first. Most are NOT prices: a breadth ratio, a volatility gap and a correlation percentile all have levels that change the regime when they break. Rows with kind='trend followers' are where systematic funds turn from buyer to seller, and any row with quotable_as_contract false carries a tracking fund's price rather than the contract's.
how_to_read.limits: What was missing or degraded in this run. Read before trusting anything above.
